profiles.basis: The source disperses chemically modified and hydrolyzed CNC feed using M-110P. This plan begins with washed, already chemically isolated CNCs. It does not replace hydrolysis or describe purely mechanical CNF production. Alternative models need sample compatibility, chamber and process qualification.

The methods distinguish CNC from nanofibrillated-cellulose feeds and identify BUCHI B-290. The output is dried CNC-containing particles/agglomerates. Nanoscale individual crystals, unchanged morphology and reversible redispersion are not guaranteed. Alternative dryers require feed, solvent, containment and operating qualification.

Abstract-level evidence for static, stirred and ultrasound-assisted dispersion comparisons and the difficulty of redispersing spray-dried CNC aggregates. The sequence is a curator planning abstraction. No operating dose, sonication energy, surfactant composition or success/yield is inferred.
